verdict.rationale: The SDK documents autonomous agent execution: the loop repeats until the task is complete without manual intervention, it can run as a long-lived process, it can be hosted in production on Docker or Kubernetes, and permission modes pre-approve actions. A community user also reports building a headless automated workflow on `claude -p`. However, nothing documents a scheduler, trigger, or recurring-run mechanism, so background automations that recur would have to be orchestrated externally. Missing for 10: built-in scheduling or recurring triggers, documented background or daemon run setup within the SDK itself, and independent hands-on corroboration of unattended background operation.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can set up automations that run autonomously in the background

citations.quote: Use the Agent SDK to build an AI agent that reads your code, finds bugs, and fixes them, all without manual intervention.
It allows the agent to operate as a long lived process that takes in user input, handles interruptions, surfaces permission requests, and handles session management.
Deploy the Agent SDK in production: subprocess architecture, session persistence, scaling, observability, and multi-tenant isolation for Docker, Kubernetes, and sandbox providers.
Use permission modes and rules to define what's allowed automatically
I built an entire headless automated workflow around `claude -p`
